Evaluating a model before deployment involves assessing its performance using available training and validation data. This evaluation helps in understanding how well the model performs on unseen data similar to the training data. However, this evaluation does not guarantee how the model will perform in the real-world setting after deployment.

After deployment, the model's performance is evaluated in the actual production environment where it interacts with real users or processes real-time data. This evaluation can reveal issues that were not apparent during the pre-deployment phase, such as changes in data distribution, unexpected user behavior, or environmental factors that affect model performance. Thus, the key difference lies in the context and the data used for evaluation: pre-deployment evaluation uses training and validation data, while post-deployment evaluation uses real-world data.
